summary: Backend-only regression + targeted verification of the deployment-resilience fix (ensure_indexes swallowing OperationFailure, on_startup wrapping each step in try/except). Ran full existing suite against the public preview URL: 80/80 passed (previously 79/80 — the DELETE /api/me/photos/{id} 404 bug is now fixed and its test passes). Added 4 new unit tests (/app/backend/tests/test_startup_resilience.py) that inject OperationFailure(code 13) and ServerSelectionTimeoutError into every create_index call and force all three startup steps to raise: ensure_indexes() and on_startup() both complete without raising, and all 3 steps are still attempted (no early abort). Total 84/84 passed. Live spot-checks: GET /api/health -> {ok:true}; GET /api/subscriptions/plans -> 3 seeded plans (1_semaine/1_mois/12_mois); admin login with identifier=Admin@sawalismartsystems.com returns JWT with role=admin; GET /api/auth/me with that token returns the bootstrapped admin (verification_status=verified); duplicate register still returns 409 (app-level uniqueness). Backend logs show 'Application startup complete' with no index/seed warnings (mongomock has no perms restrictions). No 500s anywhere. No regressions detected.

minor.issue: Recurring log warning 'Pydantic serializer warnings: Expected `enum` but got `str`' on auth/me and admin responses — models store gender/role as plain strings (seed uses model_dump(mode='json')) while the response schema declares Enum types. Cosmetic but noisy; align the model field types or coerce on read.

Catches every OperationFailure, not only code 13 (Unauthorized). In production this would also silently swallow IndexOptionsConflict (85) or a duplicate-key failure while building a unique index on already-duplicated data — the app boots but silently loses uniqueness. Consider logging at ERROR level (or re-checking exc.code) so such cases are visible in production logs.
Still exposes neither email nor phone (carried over from iteration_1) — frontend cannot display the account's own contact info.
Reload watches /app/backend/**, so adding tests/*.py restarts the app and wipes the mongomock in-memory DB. Consider --reload-exclude 'tests/*' (test-infra impact only).

action_items: Optional: log skipped indexes at ERROR (or distinguish exc.code == 13) so non-permission index failures in production Atlas are not silently swallowed.
Optional: fix the Pydantic 'Expected enum but got str' serializer warnings (seed/User stores role/gender as str).
Carried over from iteration_1 (still open): expose email/phone on /api/auth/me if the profile screen needs it; add 'autre' to models.Gender if the spec requires it.
critical_code_review_comments: server.on_startup catches bare Exception per step — intentional and correct for boot resilience, but since ensure_admin_user can now silently fail in production, the back-office could become inaccessible with only a WARNING in the logs. Consider surfacing startup step status via /api/health (e.g. {ok:true, startup:{indexes:'skipped', admin:'ok'}}) so deployment can be validated.

Uniqueness now depends entirely on the application-level find_one-before-insert in routes/auth.py when indexes are skipped; two concurrent registrations with the same email can both succeed in production. Acceptable for Phase 1, but document it.
Minor: 'import logging' inside on_startup should move to module level.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral mongomock data only (TEST_ users test_*@example.com / TestPass#2026, photos, one match+conversation, ratings, report, referral, verification, subscriptions). Wiped on next backend restart; admin + 3 plans are recreated automatically at boot (verified).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -q -p no:randomly. Do NOT create/edit files under /app/backend while a run is in progress (uvicorn --reload wipes mongomock; session-scoped fixtures are interdependent — TestMatching creates the match TestChat consumes, keep -p no:randomly, no xdist). Login field is 'identifier'. Admin review endpoints take 'approve' as a QUERY param. pytest-asyncio is NOT installed — async unit tests must use asyncio.run(). Frontend has never been tested in iterations 1-2.
rca_of_the_issue: Production crash was pymongo OperationFailure code 13 (Atlas user has readWrite but not createIndex) raised from ensure_indexes inside the FastAPI startup hook, which aborts app boot. Fix verified: db._safe_create_index catches OperationFailure/PyMongoError and logs a warning; server.on_startup wraps each of the 3 steps in try/except. Unit tests injecting OperationFailure(13) and ServerSelectionTimeoutError confirm neither ensure_indexes() nor on_startup() propagates, and all 3 steps are still attempted.
